fit: Extra Trees ranks first by training-fold RMSE (0.582 ± 0.222, versus 5.103 for the mean baseline). On the holdout it records MAE 0.381, RMSE 0.486 and R² 0.993. Errors are in thousands of sales units.
cleaning: Cleaning retained 200 of 200 markets after excluding the sequential index. It removed 0 invalid rows and 0 duplicates, and retained 2 IQR-flagged markets.
nonlinear: Adding the TV × Radio interaction changes mean validation RMSE from 1.649 to 0.943. The additive three-channel OLS records 1.664. The interaction tests whether a channel’s predictive relationship varies with the level of the other channel.
channel_strength: TV has the largest absolute standardized coefficient. Newspaper has the smallest, and its HC3 95% interval (-0.014 to 0.019) includes zero. The largest holdout permutation effect belongs to TV.
residuals: Mean holdout residual is -0.047 thousand units. Spearman correlation of residual with prediction is +0.16 (p = 0.333). The largest absolute miss is 1.19 at source row 67 (zero-based). Winner train-fold RMSE averages 0.001 versus 0.582 on validation folds. The near-zero training error shows the flexibility of the fit. Holdout RMSE (0.486) is close to validation RMSE, and the residuals show little monotone trend.
recommendations: Prioritize TV in controlled budget tests and vary TV and Radio jointly. The interaction model reduced validation error relative to the additive model.
Audit Newspaper against reach, cost and campaign objectives. The selected model uses TV, Radio, so varying Newspaper alone leaves its predictions unchanged.
At the same total budget, the scenario “Move 20% of Newspaper to Radio” yields a predicted gain of 0.99 thousand units. Pilot the reallocation while tracking incremental sales.
Among the tested spend increases, TV +20% produces the largest supported gain (+0.97 thousand units). Compare the cost and incremental sales in a controlled test.
Capture campaign dates, prices, promotions and audience segments so future models can test seasonality and segment response.
limitations: The file covers 200 historical markets and has no calendar or segment identifiers. Estimates apply to budget scenarios for comparable markets.
Market-level associations can reflect omitted variables such as pricing, promotions or market size. Use randomized tests to estimate incremental effects.
Scenario predictions are point estimates. The range and nearest-neighbor flags measure coverage of the training data and provide no prediction interval.
Repeated CV folds overlap, and tuning and ranking share those folds. The holdout provides the final evaluation and contains only 40 markets.
